chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from one of his companions, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We hear the Verses in the Quran, but they are not with us exactly as we hear them, nor do we recite them perfectly as it reached us from you. So, are we sinning?' He said, 'No. Recite as you have learned, and there will come to you one who will teach you.'
ai.seo_question: Are we sinful if our Quran recitation is not perfect?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia principle of *takhyir* (flexibility) in Quranic recitation, affirming that laypeople are not sinful for reciting according to their learned method (*qira'ah*) even if it differs from the perfect transmission. It specifically links this pedagogical patience to the eschatological role of the Qaim (Imam al-Mahdi), who will perfect their understanding and recitation upon his reappearance. This underscores the continuity between the Imam's guidance in the present age and his ultimate role as the perfect teacher in the future.
